topic: What makes top-tier US professor personal websites feel hand-crafted and timeless rather than templated — extracted from raw HTML/CSS of 39 real sites (MIT, Stanford, Berkeley, Princeton, Columbia, UW, CMU, Duke, UCSD, Cornell) plus craft references and the two dominant academic templates to avoid.
key_findings: MEASURE IS THE SINGLE STRONGEST SIGNAL. Every site that reads as crafted caps its text column tightly, and the good ones do it in em, not px: Matt Might (matt.might.net/css/mm2.css) uses `div#main { max-width: 35em }` with Palatino at 125% (=20px) — that is ~65 characters. Julia Evans (jvns.ca/stylesheets/screen.css) uses `#wrap { width: 70%; max-width: 45em }`. Tufte CSS sets the text column to `width: 55%` of an 87.5%-wide body. Amy Ko's SvelteKit CSS caps content at `max-width: 40em` inside an `80em` page shell. Contrast: the templated sites (al-folio, Minimal Mistakes) run 1140px Bootstrap containers with 16px text = ~110 characters, which is what makes them feel like a brochure.

SPECIFIC NUMBERS FROM REAL SITES, verbatim from their CSS. Karpathy (karpathy.ai/style.css): `.container { width: 970px }`, body `font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.4; color: #333`, `h1 { font-size: 34px; font-weight: normal }`, `h2 { font-size: 18px; font-style: italic; color: #999; max-width: 300px }`. David Blei (cs.columbia.edu/~blei/static/blei.css): `main { max-width: 800px }`, nav inner `max-width: 900px`, `line-height: 1.6`, tokens `--text:#111; --muted:#666; --accent:#005fa3`. Pascal Michaillat: `--main-width: 680px; --content-size: 1.125rem; --line-height: 1.5; --primary: rgb(30,30,30); --secondary: rgb(108,108,108); --tertiary: rgb(165,165,165); --border: rgb(230,230,230)`. UW Interactive Data Lab (idl.uw.edu): `max-width: 56rem` (896px). Tufte: `html { font-size: 15px }` with `p { font-size: 1.4rem; line-height: 2rem }` = 21px/30px.

OFF-WHITE PAPER GROUND, NEVER PURE #FFF, is the fastest way to look designed. Tufte CSS: `background-color: #fffff8; color: #111` (a warm ivory). Maggie Appleton: `--color-cream: #f6f5f1`, `--color-light-cream: #fcfbf7`, and text is `--color-black: #353534`, not #000. Matt Might sets body `color: #505050`. Nadia Polikarpova (cseweb.ucsd.edu/~npolikarpova/styles/ucsd.css) inverts it: `body { background-color: #ebecee }` with a white content panel floating on it. Templates ship #ffffff on #000000 and read as a default.

PUBLICATIONS ARE NEVER CARDS ON THE GOOD SITES — they are hairline-ruled or left-ruled text blocks. Karpathy's CSS literally has `.pub { font-size: 14px; border-left: 4px solid #aaa; padding: 2px 0 2px 10px }` — a rule, not a box. Jeff Heer's `.entry { clear: both; height: 80px }` with a `float: left` thumbnail and no border at all. Blei's publications are a plain `<ul class="bib2xhtml">` with `list-style: disc inside`. Michael Bernstein and Maneesh Agrawala both use thumbnail-left + title/authors/venue-right rows with no container chrome. Card shadows appear only in the templated sites.

THE ONE-ACCENT-COLOUR RULE IS REAL AND THE ACCENT IS USUALLY UNUSUAL, NOT BLUE. Jeff Heer (jheer.css): all links are `color: #000` with no underline, and hover flips to `#53f` — a blue-violet — plus `.entry a:hover img { box-shadow: 2px 2px 18px #53f }`, so colour appears only on interaction. Julia Evans uses burnt orange `#CC4B00` for links and `#FF5E00` for title links. Polikarpova uses purple `#50416d` links on a `#5d4e79` nav bar. Michael Bernstein uses Stanford cardinal `#990615` links with `#7D0612` navbar. Blei uses exactly one: `--accent: #005fa3`. Maggie Appleton runs two: `--color-sea-blue: #04a5bb` and `--color-crimson: #5f023e`.

AN ASYMMETRIC HERO BEATS A CENTERED ONE. Karpathy: a 12-column grid where `#dpic { grid-column: span 6; text-align: right }` holds a 240x240 `border-radius: 120px` headshot, and `#ddesc { grid-column: span 6; padding-top: 40px }` — note the 40px top padding, which optically aligns the name to the middle of the photo rather than its top edge. Tim Roughgarden (timroughgarden.org) goes the other way: a 620x420 LANDSCAPE environmental photo on the left, name/affiliations/contact on the right, whole page 2.5KB. The centered-avatar-above-centered-name arrangement is the PaperMod/al-folio giveaway.

A PHOTO CREDIT LINE IS A DISPROPORTIONATELY STRONG HUMANITY SIGNAL. Roughgarden captions his portrait `Photo credit: Diane Bondareff`. Hal Abelson (groups.csail.mit.edu/mac/users/hal/) has `
Portrait by Joi Ito
` under his photo. Nobody's template does this; it costs one line and immediately reads as a real person with real photographs.

TYPEFACE CHOICES THAT SIGNAL SCHOLARSHIP. Chris Olah (colah.github.io) self-hosts Computer Modern — `fonts/Serif/cmun-serif.css` defines `@font-face { font-family: 'CMS'; src: url('cmunrm.woff') }` (cmunrm/cmunbx/cmunti/cmunbi = roman/bold/italic/bold-italic) — i.e. the LaTeX typeface on the web. gwern.net uses Source Serif 4 + Source Sans 3 + IBM Plex Mono. Tufte CSS uses ET Book with the fallback stack `et-book, Palatino, "Palatino Linotype", "Palatino LT STD", "Book Antiqua", Georgia, serif`. Julia Evans pairs PT Serif body with Montserrat headings. Maggie Appleton pairs Canela Text (body) + Canela Deck (display) + Lato (sans). Templated sites all default to Roboto/Roboto Slab (al-folio) or Lato/Open Sans/Montserrat with Font Awesome.

SECTION HEADINGS AS SMALL CAPS WITH LETTERSPACING, NOT AS BIG BOLD SANS. Jeff Heer repurposes `h6` as his section header: `h6 { font-size: 1.5em; font-weight: normal; font-variant: small-caps; letter-spacing: 1px; color: #777; line-height: 0.60em }` — light grey, normal weight, small caps. His name uses `#name { font-variant: small-caps; font-size: 1.5em; letter-spacing: 0.065em }`. That single decision does more for the page's character than any hero image.

A YEAR GUTTER + VERTICAL RAIL IS THE BEST 'CAREER / NEWS' PATTERN I FOUND. Karpathy's timeline: `.timespan { grid-column: span 1; font-size: 14px; text-align: right; color: #bbb }` (right-aligned year in its own column), then `.ico { grid-column: span 1; border-left: 2px solid #cfcfcf; position: relative }` and `.entry-dot { position: absolute; left: -8px; width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 7px; background-color: #cfcfcf; border: 2px solid white }` — the 2px white ring is what makes the dot sit ON the rail. Jeff Heer's CV uses the same idea flat: `#vita .margin { float: left; width: 115px; text-align: right }` with `#vita .body { margin-left: 135px }`.

HAIRLINE DIVIDERS DONE WITH INTENT. Karpathy's `hr` is not a line, it is a fading gradient: `background-image: linear-gradient(left, rgba(0,0,0,0), rgba(0,0,0,0.75), rgba(0,0,0,0)); height: 1px; border: 0; margin: 20px 0`. Maneesh Agrawala (graphics.stanford.edu/~maneesh/) separates sections with typographic asterisk rules. Blei's only chrome in the entire site is `border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd` under the nav. That is the whole vocabulary: hairlines, gradients-to-transparent, whitespace.

SIDENOTES / MARGIN NOTES ARE THE HIGHEST-CRAFT MOVE AND ARE CHEAP. Tufte CSS: `.sidenote, .marginnote { float: right; clear: right; margin-right: -60%; width: 50%; font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1.3 }` with an auto-numbering `counter-reset: sidenote-counter` and `content: counter(sidenote-counter)` — and below 760px they collapse to tap-to-reveal toggles. gwern caps them at `--GW-sidenotes-max-width: 550px`. gwern also adds `.heading a::after { content: "\00B6" }` (a pilcrow section self-link) at 0.75em.

SIDEBAR-NAV-WITH-SCROLLSPY IS THE ONE 'CHROME' PATTERN THAT STILL LOOKS GOOD, IF THE ACTIVE STATE IS A RULE NOT A PILL. Michael Bernstein (hci.stanford.edu/msb/css/msb.css): `.sidenav .nav > li > a { padding: 5px 20px }` and on hover/active `background-color: #e5e3e9; border-right: 1px solid #990615`. A 1px accent rule on the active item — no rounded pill, no filled chip.

INLINE COLLABORATOR AVATARS IN AUTHOR LISTS. Michael Bernstein embeds tiny student photos next to student names inside each publication's author line, and Amy Ko puts a horizontal row of ~50-60px circular collaborator headshots beneath each research 'discovery'. It ties the pubs list to the people page without a separate section and reads as generous rather than self-promoting.

GROUPING PUBLICATIONS BY VENUE-AND-PLACE HEADER, NOT JUST YEAR. UW Interactive Data Lab (idl.uw.edu) heads its paper groups with e.g. 'VIS 2025 - Vienna, Austria' and alternates the thumbnail left/right down the list. That single alternation removes the spreadsheet feeling from a long list at zero design cost.

A JUSTIFIED NAVIGATION BAR — a genuinely unusual, hand-made detail. Arvind Narayanan (cs.princeton.edu/~arvindn/) does it with pure CSS: `#navbar { text-align: justify; width: 980px } #navbar a { display: inline-block } #navbar:after { content: ''; width: 100%; display: inline-block }`. The links spread edge to edge like a masthead. He also runs an oversized lead paragraph: `p.lead { font-size: 144%; line-height: 150% }`.

THE HEADSHOT IS SMALL AND OFTEN LIVES IN THE NAV, NOT IN A HERO. Blei's entire nav is name + affiliation + email on the left and a `75px` circular `object-fit: cover` avatar on the right, above a single `1px #ddd` rule — and the whole homepage HTML is 2,819 bytes. Michaillat's PaperMod profile uses `height=130 width=130`. Karpathy's 240px is the largest I found on a crafted site. Jeff Heer's homepage has NO photo of himself at all.

MOBILE IS HANDLED WITH ONE OR TWO BREAKPOINTS, NOT A FRAMEWORK. Karpathy has exactly two: `@media (min-width: 992px)` sets the 970px container, `@media (max-width: 991px)` flips his 6/6 hero to 12/12 and centers it, and `.hassets { display: none }` drops decorative assets entirely on mobile. Tufte uses one at 760px. gwern uses one at 649px. Blei's only media query is `@media (max-width: 320px)`. Fewer breakpoints, chosen deliberately, read better than a 5-tier grid.

WHAT THE TEMPLATES ACTUALLY LOOK LIKE, so you can avoid the fingerprint. al-folio (alshedivat.github.io/al-folio) loads Tailwind + `fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Roboto:300,400,500,700|Roboto+Slab:100,300,400,500,700|Material+Icons` + Font Awesome 7.2 + academicons 1.9.5 + scholar-icons 1.0.3 + a light/dark highlight-theme swap. academicpages (Minimal Mistakes) ships `author__avatar`, `author__bio`, `author__urls social-icons`, `greedy-nav` — the sticky left author sidebar with a stack of round social icons. Both are instantly recognisable to anyone who has seen ten academic sites.

THE HEAVY-CMS FAILURE MODE, measured. Daniela Rus (danielarus.csail.mit.edu) is Avada WordPress + RevSlider and ships 1,436,528 bytes of HTML for a homepage. Regina Barzilay (people.csail.mit.edu/regina/) is Wix — 548,929 bytes, fonts named `wf_34f7b8ddea86409f84985334d` and `din-next-w01-light`. Karpathy's whole site is 34,286 bytes of HTML plus one hand-written stylesheet, with the comment in his own words: '0 frameworks were used to make this simple responsive website because I am becoming seriously allergic to 500-pound websites.'

DOMAIN CHECK — the hydrology/climate field has almost no well-designed personal sites, which is an opportunity. Roxy Mathew Koll's Climate Research Lab (climate.rocksea.org) is the WordPress 'hueman' theme; Patrick Reed's group (reed.cee.cornell.edu) is the WordPress 'aaron' theme; Deepti Singh's Climate Extremes Lab (deeptis47.github.io) is Montserrat + Font Awesome + academicons, i.e. the academic-template look; Peter Webster (webster.eas.gatech.edu) is a 2.9KB hand-rolled page with a lightbox; Dara Entekhabi and Steven Gorelick have no personal site at all, only institutional profile pages (cee.mit.edu, profiles.stanford.edu). A genuinely typographic hydrology site would be close to unique in the field.
recommendations: SET THE MEASURE FIRST AND IN EM. Body prose column at `max-width: 34em` (≈62-68 characters), page shell at `max-width: 72rem` for the wider hero/publication/people rows. Do not use a 1140px Bootstrap container. If you want a single number: 660-700px of prose, matching Michaillat's `--main-width: 680px` and Might's `35em`.

PICK A WARM PAPER GROUND AND OFF-BLACK INK. Something like `--paper: #fbfaf7` / `--ink: #1e1c1a` / `--ink-muted: #6b6660` / `--rule: #e5e2dc`. Never `#ffffff` on `#000000`. Tufte's `#fffff8` and Appleton's `#f6f5f1` are the proven references; a hydrology site can lean very slightly cool-grey instead of ivory without losing the effect.

USE A SERIF FOR BODY PROSE AT 19-20px with 1.6-1.65 line-height, and a sans only for labels, metadata, nav and captions. Concrete, freely available pairing that will not read as template: Source Serif 4 (gwern's choice, and it is on Google Fonts) for body + Inter or Söhne-alike grotesque for UI, or the more distinctive Newsreader / Literata / Spectral for body. Avoid Roboto, Roboto Slab, Lato, Montserrat, Open Sans and Poppins entirely — those five ARE the academic-template palette (al-folio ships Roboto + Roboto Slab, academicpages and Deepti Singh's lab ship Montserrat/Lato).

ONE ACCENT, AND MAKE IT UNEXPECTED. Given hydrology, resist default corporate blue — everyone in water uses it. Consider a deep monsoon indigo (#2b3a67-ish) or a silt/ochre (#9a5b2c-ish) as the single accent, with links rendered as ink-coloured text carrying a 1px accent underline that thickens on hover, the way Jeff Heer keeps links black until hover then flips to #53f. One accent, used for links, active nav state, and nothing else.

HERO: ASYMMETRIC, WITH A REAL PHOTOGRAPH AND A CREDIT. Two options, both verified in the wild: (a) Karpathy's split — headshot right-aligned in a 5/12 column at ~200-240px with `border-radius: 50%`, name + one-sentence positioning line left, with ~40px top padding on the text so the name optically centers against the photo; or (b) Roughgarden's — a wide landscape field/river/flood photograph from Prof. Regonda's own fieldwork on the left, name and affiliations on the right. Option (b) is stronger for a hydrologist and is almost never seen. Caption the photo with place and year ('Godavari basin, 2023') — that one line is worth more than any hero animation.

PUBLICATIONS: HAIRLINE ROWS, NEVER CARDS. Each entry as `padding: 1.1rem 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule)`, with the year in a right-aligned 4rem gutter column (Heer's `#vita .margin { float: left; width: 115px; text-align: right }` pattern), title in body serif at 1rem, authors in sans at 0.875rem muted with Prof. Regonda's own name in medium weight, venue in italic, and PDF/DOI/Code/Data as small caps links. Zero `box-shadow` anywhere in the stylesheet — make that a rule you can grep for.

GROUP THE PUBLICATION LIST BY YEAR WITH A STICKY YEAR LABEL in the left gutter rather than repeating a big centered '2024' heading, and offer a quiet filter row (All / Journal / Conference / Reports) rendered as text links with an underline on active — not as pill buttons. IDL's venue-and-place group headers ('VIS 2025 - Vienna, Austria') are worth stealing for conference entries.

NEWS / UPDATES: build it as Karpathy's rail — a `2px solid var(--rule)` vertical line, `10px` dots with a `2px solid var(--paper)` ring at `left: -8px`, and a right-aligned year or month in a narrow left column at 0.8rem muted. This is the single most 'hand-made-looking' component you can ship, it is about 15 lines of CSS, and it maps perfectly onto a Google Sheet with columns date | headline | link.

SECTION HEADINGS IN SMALL CAPS: `font-variant: small-caps; letter-spacing: 0.08em; font-weight: 400; color: var(--ink-muted); font-size: 0.95rem` above a hairline rule. This is Jeff Heer's `h6` trick and it is the cheapest way to look edited rather than generated. Reserve actual large type for the page title only.

ADD MARGIN NOTES TO THE BLOG AND THE RAFT PAGE. Implement Tufte's pattern verbatim (`float: right; clear: right; margin-right: -60%; width: 50%; font-size: 0.9em; line-height: 1.35`) with a `@media (max-width: 900px)` fallback that renders them inline as an indented aside. Use them for definitions (what a 'return period' is), dataset citations, and asides — it makes a hydrology blog feel like a book, and no competing academic site in the field has it.

NAVIGATION: a single top bar of 5-7 plain text links, ink-coloured, with the active item carrying a 1px accent underline offset ~6px. No logo lockup, no hamburger on desktop, no dropdown menus, no sticky-with-shadow-on-scroll. If Prof. Regonda wants his name in the bar, set it in small caps with letterspacing (Heer's `#name`) rather than as a bold sans wordmark.

MOTION: budget exactly two effects and no more — (1) a link underline that grows from 1px to 2px over 150ms, or Appleton's clip-path underline reveal (`transition: clip-path .3s, transform .3s cubic-bezier(.2,1,.8,1)`); (2) a 400ms fade-up on first paint for the hero only, gated behind `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. No scroll-triggered reveals, no counters, no parallax, no AOS library. Scroll-reveal on every section is the loudest AI/template tell there is.

FOOTER: three lines, left-aligned, at 0.8rem muted — postal address block (Dept. of Civil Engineering, IIT Hyderabad, Kandi, Sangareddy 502284), a link row (Google Scholar / ORCID / RAFT / CV), and a 'Last updated <date>' stamp pulled from the Sheet's modified time. Heer's footer is literally one lab image plus 'Visit the UW Interactive Data Lab for more! >>' — that kind of single-purpose footer is what confident sites do. No newsletter box, no back-to-top button, no social icon grid.

GIVE THE RAFT PAGE A DIFFERENT RHYTHM FROM THE PERSONAL PAGES so it reads as a place, not a tab: one full-bleed field photograph, a two-sentence mission line set at ~1.4x body size (Arvind Narayanan's `p.lead { font-size: 144% }`), then people as a plain grid of square-cropped photos with name + role + one-line focus underneath — no cards, no hover lift — then a single prominent outbound link to raftwaters.in styled as a text link with an arrow, not a button.

ENFORCE THE RESTRAINT MECHANICALLY. Write the whole thing as one hand-authored stylesheet with ~14 CSS custom properties (paper, ink, ink-muted, rule, accent, accent-tint, font-serif, font-sans, measure, space-2xs…space-2xl) and adopt these bans as lint rules: no `border-radius` above 4px except circular avatars, no `box-shadow` at all, no gradient backgrounds, no icon font (inline the 4-6 SVGs you need), no more than 2 typefaces plus a mono, no more than 2 media queries. Karpathy's entire site is one 34KB HTML file plus one hand-written CSS file; that constraint is the aesthetic.

TYPE SCALE, ready to use: body 19px/1.62; small/meta 15px; lead 26px/1.4; h3 21px small-caps; h2 28px; h1 40px at weight 400 (not 700 — Tufte sets `h1 { font-weight: 400; font-size: 3.2rem; line-height: 1 }` and Karpathy sets `h1 { font-size: 34px; font-weight: normal }`; normal-weight large headings are a consistent marker of the crafted sites). Optionally make it fluid with the Utopia approach Appleton uses (body clamps 20→22px between her min and max viewport).

SPEND THE DESIGN BUDGET ON ONE SIGNATURE ELEMENT, not on five. Candidates in priority order: (1) the news/CV timeline rail; (2) margin notes on the blog; (3) a small recurring hydrograph/basin-outline motif drawn as inline SVG in the accent colour, used once per section as a divider — the equivalent of gwern's asterisms and Japanese-crest ornaments, which he ships as data-URI SVG custom properties. One memorable, field-specific mark beats a general-purpose 'modern' look.

TEST AGAINST THE TWO TEMPLATES BEFORE SHIPPING. Open alshedivat.github.io/al-folio and academicpages.github.io side by side with the draft. If the draft shares any of: Roboto/Lato/Montserrat, a round social-icon strip, card grids with shadows, a dark-mode toggle in the top-right, or an avatar centered above a centered name — change it. Those five features are the template fingerprint.

exemplars.name: Andrej Karpathy (formerly Stanford / OpenAI / Tesla)
exemplars.what_works: 970px container, 12-col grid, asymmetric 6/6 hero with a 240px circular headshot right-aligned and the name block given 40px top padding so it optically centers. The career history is a vertical timeline built from a 2px #cfcfcf left rule plus 10px dots with a 2px white ring, and a right-aligned 14px #bbb year gutter. Publications are `border-left: 4px solid #aaa` blocks, never cards. The `hr` is a gradient that fades to transparent at both ends. Two media queries total; decorative assets are simply `display: none` on mobile. Entire site: 34KB HTML + one hand-written stylesheet, zero frameworks.
exemplars.steal_this: The timeline rail — `.ico { border-left: 2px solid #cfcfcf; position: relative }` with `.entry-dot { position:absolute; left:-8px; width:10px; height:10px; border-radius:7px; background:#cfcfcf; border:2px solid white }` and a right-aligned year column. It maps one-to-one onto a Google Sheet (date | headline | link) and is the single most hand-made-looking component you can ship for News/Career.

exemplars.name: Jeffrey Heer (University of Washington, Interactive Data Lab)
exemplars.what_works: No headshot at all. Fixed 960px with a 210px float-left info rail and `#main { margin-left: 230px }`. Links are `color: #000` with no underline until hover, when they flip to `#53f`; visited rows go `#888` so you can see what you've already read. Section headers are `h6` set as `font-variant: small-caps; letter-spacing: 1px; font-weight: normal; color: #777`. Project entries are fixed-height 80px rows with a float-left thumbnail and no border. The CV uses a 115px right-aligned year margin column. Footer is one lab image and one sentence.
exemplars.steal_this: Two things: (1) `h6`-as-section-rule — small caps, letterspaced, normal weight, muted grey, which instantly reads 'edited' rather than 'generated'; and (2) the ink-coloured link that only reveals the accent colour on hover, so the page is monochrome at rest.

exemplars.name: David Blei (Columbia University)
exemplars.what_works: A 2,819-byte homepage. Fully tokenised CSS (`--text:#111; --muted:#666; --accent:#005fa3` plus a four-step space scale), `main { max-width: 800px }`, `line-height: 1.6`. The nav IS the header: name + affiliation + email on the left, a 75px circular `object-fit: cover` avatar on the right, section links below, and the only chrome in the entire site is a `1px solid #ddd` bottom border. Publications render as a plain `<ul>`. One media query, at 320px.
exemplars.steal_this: The nav-as-identity-block: name, affiliation, email and a small circular photo in a single hairline-ruled bar, with no hero section at all. It gives you a persistent identity on every page for about 20 lines of markup — perfect for a modular multi-page academic site.

exemplars.name: Edward Tufte / Dave Liepmann — Tufte CSS
exemplars.what_works: `background-color: #fffff8` warm paper with `#111` ink. `html { font-size: 15px }`, body prose at `1.4rem/2rem` (21px/30px) in ET Book/Palatino, text column at 55% of body width. `h1 { font-weight: 400 }`, `h2` and `h3` in italic at weight 400. Auto-numbered sidenotes via `counter-reset` that float into the right margin at `margin-right: -60%; width: 50%`, and collapse to tap-toggles below 760px. Full-width figures escape the measure with `figure.fullwidth`.
exemplars.steal_this: The margin-note system, verbatim, plus the `#fffff8` paper ground and italic-normal-weight subheads. On a hydrology blog, sidenotes for definitions, dataset citations and caveats will look like a book and will be unique in the field.

exemplars.name: Maggie Appleton (independent, ex-Normally/Egghead)
exemplars.what_works: Serif-for-everything editorial system: Canela Text for body, Canela Deck for display, Lato only for UI. Cream grounds (#f6f5f1 / #fcfbf7 / #e6e3e1) with off-black #353534 ink. Two accents — sea blue #04a5bb and crimson #5f023e — with `color-mix()` tints derived from them rather than hand-picked. Utopia fluid type: body 20→22px, headings 25→28.6, 30→36, 39→44, 46.9→56, 57.6→81.8. Six-stop layered box-shadows instead of the CSS default. Complete dark-mode token pairs.
exemplars.steal_this: Two things: the fluid type scale numbers (body clamped 20→22px is the right size for an editorial academic site) and the clip-path link underline that unrolls on hover — `transition: clip-path .3s, transform .3s cubic-bezier(.2,1,.8,1)` on a 1px `:before` bar at `top: 95%`. It is the entire motion budget the site needs.

exemplars.name: Tim Roughgarden (Institute for Advanced Study / Columbia)
exemplars.what_works: The whole page is 2,568 bytes: a 620x420 landscape photograph on the left credited `<small>Photo credit: Diane Bondareff</small>`, name/affiliations/research-interests/contact on the right, a rule, then a flat `<ul>` of eleven destinations. Body is Helvetica with `p { font-size: 18px }` and nothing else. It reads as completely confident because it makes no attempt to impress.
exemplars.steal_this: The landscape-photo hero with a caption credit, instead of a circular avatar. For a hydrologist this becomes a field photograph — a gauging station, a flooded street, a Godavari reach — captioned with place and year. Almost no academic site does this and it immediately says 'this person does fieldwork'.

exemplars.name: Michael Bernstein (Stanford HCI)
exemplars.what_works: Helvetica Neue at weight 300/16px, one accent (Stanford cardinal #990615 for links, #7D0612 for the bar), and a sticky sidenav with scrollspy whose active state is `background-color:#e5e3e9; border-right: 1px solid #990615` — a hairline, not a pill. Publications run 2026→2024 as thumbnail-left rows. The distinguishing content move: student names inside each publication's author list carry tiny inline portrait avatars, and the page ends with current PhD students, alumni and postdoc alumni as photo rows.
exemplars.steal_this: Inline student avatars in author lists, and the 1px-accent-rule active nav state. The avatars connect the publications section to the people section without duplicating anything, and they read as generous rather than self-promoting — exactly the tone a PI running the RAFT group wants.

exemplars.name: UW Interactive Data Lab (Jeffrey Heer's group)
exemplars.what_works: Self-hosted Avenir across six weights, `max-width: 56rem` (896px), essentially monochrome. Papers are grouped under venue-and-place headers ('VIS 2025 - Vienna, Austria') rather than bare years, each row is thumbnail + linked title + linked author names + venue + PDF/Software/Examples, and the thumbnails alternate left/right down the list. A 'Spotlight' feature project sits above the paper list; courses split Graduate/Undergraduate; a dated updates feed sits below.
exemplars.steal_this: The whole information architecture for the RAFT page: one spotlight project on top, then papers grouped by venue-and-place with left/right alternating thumbnails, then courses, then a dated updates feed. The alternation alone removes the spreadsheet feeling from a long publication list for free.

exemplars.name: Arvind Narayanan (Princeton)
exemplars.what_works: 980px, Open Sans 400/600, an oversized lead paragraph at `font-size: 144%; line-height: 150%`, and a two-column body of 460px widgets with a 60px gutter — an editorial spread with the book cover floating left and a figure floating right, not a card grid. Whole page is 12.5KB with the CSS inline.
exemplars.steal_this: The pure-CSS justified navigation: `#navbar { text-align: justify; width: 980px }`, `#navbar a { display: inline-block }`, `#navbar:after { content:''; width:100%; display:inline-block }`. The links spread edge-to-edge like a newspaper masthead. Five lines, unmistakably deliberate, and I have not seen it on any template.

exemplars.name: Chris Olah (Anthropic, ex-Google Brain / Distill)
exemplars.what_works: Self-hosts Computer Modern as webfonts (cmunrm/cmunbx/cmunti/cmunbi) so the site is set in the LaTeX typeface — an immediate scholarly signal that costs nothing. The homepage is a thumbnail-per-post list organised under headings the author invented rather than inherited: 'Recent Exciting Things', 'Neural Networks (General)', 'Visualizing Neural Networks', 'Rough Notes' (explicitly labelled as lower-quality), 'Personal Writing', 'Selected Twitter Threads', 'Traditional Papers'. Content capped around 800-850px.
exemplars.steal_this: Two ideas: (1) a serif with real scholarly provenance for body text; and (2) inventing your own content categories and being honest about their quality. A hydrology blog with sections like 'Field notes', 'Rough notes', 'Explainers for non-specialists' and 'Papers' is instantly more human than 'Blog / Publications'.

exemplars.name: Matt Might (University of Alabama at Birmingham, formerly Utah)
exemplars.what_works: The entire design is three declarations: `body { font-family: Palatino; font-size: 125%; color: #505050 }` and `div#main { max-width: 35em; margin: 0 auto }`. Text at 20px in a 35em column is ~66 characters — textbook measure. Ink is #505050, not black. Blockquotes get a `10px solid #ccc` left bar and a 4em decorative opening quote mark.
exemplars.steal_this: Set the measure in `em` rather than `px` — `max-width: 35em` stays correct if you ever change the body size or typeface, whereas a px container silently breaks the line length. Also: never use pure black for body text.

exemplars.name: Julia Evans (independent; widely cited as a craft reference)
exemplars.what_works: PT Serif body at `line-height: 1.25em`, Montserrat for headings and for a bold-uppercase nav, Alegreya for the site subtitle — three typefaces with strictly separated jobs. `#wrap { width: 70%; max-width: 45em }` collapsing to 100% at 865px. The masthead h1 is a huge 4em PT Sans. One accent, burnt orange: links #CC4B00, title links #FF5E00.
exemplars.steal_this: The three-typeface job separation (serif = prose, sans = navigation and headings, mono = code/data) with an unmistakably non-default accent. Burnt orange on a serif blog is a decision; #007bff is a default.

exemplars.name: Pascal Michaillat (UC Santa Cruz) — Hugo academic template
exemplars.what_works: Clean numeric system worth copying wholesale: `--main-width: 680px`, `--nav-width: 1024px`, `--content-size: 1.125rem`, `--line-height: 1.5`, a three-step grey ramp (`--primary: rgb(30,30,30)`, `--secondary: rgb(108,108,108)`, `--tertiary: rgb(165,165,165)`) and `--border: rgb(230,230,230)`. 130px profile image, three-sentence positioning paragraph, seven inline-SVG icons, five section links. 9.2KB homepage. He publishes his LaTeX/Hugo/MATLAB templates at /design/ under a stated 'typographical best practices, minimalist design' philosophy.
exemplars.steal_this: The token values — 680px measure, 1.125rem content, 1.5 line-height, and especially the three-step grey ramp for primary/secondary/tertiary text. But NOT the layout: this is PaperMod profile mode and it is recognisable as a template. Take the numbers, invent the arrangement.

exemplars.name: Amy J. Ko (University of Washington, iSchool)
exemplars.what_works: Nunito throughout, `max-width: 40em` for text inside an `80em` shell, and an 18-item text nav with no dropdowns. The homepage organises research not as 'areas' but as dated **claims** — 'Programming languages can be designed to include everyone (2011-2026)' — each with an image, a horizontal row of ~50-60px circular collaborator headshots linked to their profiles, and a collapsed `▶ 6 publications` disclosure. The writing is plain-spoken ('Programming is hard for many reasons') without losing authority.
exemplars.steal_this: Framing research as dated claims with collaborator faces attached, rather than as topic buckets. For Prof. Regonda this becomes e.g. 'Seasonal streamflow in the Godavari can be forecast months ahead (2015-2026)' with the students who did it pictured underneath — content structure no template can hand you, and the thing that will most make the site feel authored.

pitfalls: Using Roboto, Roboto Slab, Lato, Montserrat, Open Sans or Poppins. These are literally the fonts al-folio (`Roboto:300,400,500,700|Roboto+Slab:100,300,400,500,700`), academicpages, Deepti Singh's Climate Extremes Lab (Montserrat) and Ed Chi's Google Site (Lato) load. Any one of them collapses the site into the template category on sight.

Loading an icon font — Font Awesome, academicons, scholar-icons, Material Icons. Every templated academic site in this sample loads at least two of them; not one of the crafted sites loads any. Inline the four to six SVGs you actually need (Karpathy ships six local .svg files; Michaillat inlines them in the HTML).

Cards with box-shadows and rounded corners for publications, projects or people. This is the single loudest template tell. Even Blei's one concession — `.courses li { border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 6px; background: #fafafa; transition: transform .1s }` with a `translateY(-2px)` hover — is the weakest part of his otherwise excellent site.

A centered circular avatar above a centered name above centered social icons. That exact stack is Hugo PaperMod / Hugo Blox profile mode. Michaillat's site has it and it is the only reason his page reads as a template despite the good typography. Go asymmetric or go landscape.

Full-bleed hero with an overlaid gradient and a headline in 60px bold sans. Not one of the 15+ respected professor sites uses this. It reads as a startup landing page, and in 2026 it reads specifically as AI-generated.

Scroll-triggered fade-up reveals on every section (AOS, framer-motion in-view, etc.). Zero crafted sites in this sample have them. Combined with a card grid and Inter/Poppins, this is the current signature of an LLM-authored page.

Letting the prose column run wider than ~40em. At 16px/1140px you get ~110 characters per line, which is where a page stops feeling like something a person edited. Every single crafted site here caps at 35-45em or 680-900px.
Pure #ffffff background with #000000 text. Tufte (#fffff8), Appleton (#f6f5f1), Might (#505050 ink), Polikarpova (#ebecee ground) all avoid it. It costs nothing to warm the ground by 2-3%.

A dark-mode toggle in the top-right corner. It is an al-folio default and adds a control most academic visitors never touch. If you want dark support, do it as Tufte does — a silent `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block — not as a UI affordance.

Building on WordPress or Wix to make editing easy. Measured in this sample: Daniela Rus's Avada site ships 1,436,528 bytes of homepage HTML; Regina Barzilay's Wix site 548,929 bytes with fonts named `wf_34f7b8ddea86409f84985334d`. Both belong to distinguished MIT professors and both look worse than Blei's 2,819-byte page. The Google-Sheets-to-static-build route (CSS-Tricks and Mark Hansen both document Eleventy/Hugo + published-CSV pipelines) gets the non-technical editing without the weight.

Auto-generating a 'Research Areas' grid of three or four topic tiles with stock icons. Amy Ko's dated claims, Olah's self-invented categories and Guo's numbered eras all show that inventing your own taxonomy is what makes a site feel authored. Generic buckets are what a template gives you when you gave it nothing.

Letting the blog inherit a different visual system from the rest of the site (a common failure when a blog is bolted on via a hosted service). Julia Evans, Olah and gwern all run one type system across index and article. If the blog needs a CMS, make sure the CSS is still yours.

Overloading the accent colour. Once it appears on links, buttons, section headings, borders and hover states simultaneously, it stops being an accent. Heer's discipline — everything black until hover — is the reference.

Copying gwern's or Tufte's full apparatus (link popups, ornaments, drop caps, ToC sidebars). gwern's stylesheet is 310KB and defines over forty popup and toolbar variables. Take the sidenote and pilcrow ideas; leave the machinery.

Skipping the photo credits and dates. A caption like 'Godavari basin, 2023' or 'Portrait by ___' is one line of markup and is the cheapest available proof that a real person assembled this page. Roughgarden and Abelson both do it; no template does.
